jobs.title: Dean of Academic Affairs
jobs.description:
About Franklin Switzerland Founded in 1969, Franklin Switzerland is among the first institutions to bring the U.S. liberal arts model to Europe. Located in Sorengo, overlooking Lugano and its lake in the Italian-speaking region of Switzerland, Franklin combines a residential learning community, small classes, close faculty–student engagement, interdisciplinary study, and a global outlook. Franklin is accredited in the United States by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education (MSCHE) and operates as an accredited university institute within the Swiss higher education system. A defining feature of Franklin’s curriculum is Academic Travel: faculty-designed and faculty-led study trips that connect classroom learning with international, place-based experiences. Integrated into course objectives and assessment, Academic Travel engages students directly with the historical, cultural, political, environmental, and social contexts they study. Franklin offers undergraduate and graduate programs and promotes a strong culture of teaching, scholarship, and interdisciplinary collaboration. As a university institute in Switzerland, Franklin is committed to research standards, external grant activity, and academic quality assurance. Its graduate offerings include the Master of Arts in Sustainability and Transformation and the Swiss-accredited PhD in Political Science. Franklin engages with quality frameworks administered by MSCHE, the Swiss Accreditation Council (SAC), and the Swiss Agency of Accreditation and Quality Assurance (AAQ). The Opportunity Franklin Switzerland invites applications and nominations for the position of Dean of Academic Affairs (Chief Academic Officer), with an anticipated start in July 2027 for the 2027–28 academic year. Reporting to the President and working closely with the President’s Cabinet, the Dean leads the academic programs, operations, and support functions of the institution and contributes to its strategic direction. Franklin seeks a collaborative, forward-thinking academic leader who can advance its U.S. residential liberal arts model while supporting the research, quality, and institutional expectations of Swiss and European higher education. The Dean works closely with faculty governance bodies, Associate Deans, academic program leadership, and support units to promote teaching excellence, academic innovation, faculty scholarship, and student success. The role combines strategic leadership with substantial day-to-day academic administrative responsibility. Key Responsibilities Academic Leadership and Curriculum Development
• Lead the development, periodic review, and enhancement of undergraduate and graduate academic programs, ensuring academic quality and alignment with Franklin’s mission.
• Strengthen the residential liberal arts curriculum, its interdisciplinary character, and its emphasis on active, student-centered, and experiential education.
• Support the continued development and full academic integration of Franklin’s signature Academic Travel program, including its connections to course learning outcomes.
• Guide proposals for new academic programs and curricular initiatives in response to institutional priorities and emerging educational needs. Faculty Development and Pedagogy
• Promote teaching excellence through faculty development in active liberal arts learning, effective curriculum design, and student-centered pedagogy.
• Encourage innovative teaching approaches suited to a diverse, international, residential learning community.
• Foster interdisciplinary collaboration, faculty exchange, and a collegial and intellectually engaged academic culture. Faculty Leadership and Shared Governance
• Collaborate with faculty governance bodies and committees on academic policies and shared-governance processes.
• Oversee faculty evaluation, promotion, and professional development processes in partnership with the appropriate faculty committees.
• Provide academic leadership and support for faculty work, while encouraging productive relationships across academic divisions and programs. Student Success and Academic Support
• Partner with the Associate Dean for Student Success and colleagues across the institution to strengthen advising, learning support, and academic policies that promote student success.
• Ensure effective academic support systems, including academic advising, learning assistance, and appropriate academic accommodations, consistent with a U.S.-style residential liberal arts environment.
• Work with academic support units and student services to address student academic concerns and maintain a responsive, supportive learning environment. Research and Scholarly Engagement
• Support a vibrant culture of faculty research and scholarship across disciplines, consistent with the expectations of a Swiss university institute and the broader international academic community.
• Encourage applications for competitive research funding, major external grants, and research partnerships.
• Provide academic leadership for research-related programs, including Franklin’s Swiss-accredited PhD in Political Science.
• Promote interdisciplinary research addressing global challenges, including sustainability and social impact. Institutional Effectiveness and Accreditation
• Lead academic assessment, institutional effectiveness, and evidence-informed continuous improvement in partnership with the Associate Dean for Institutional Effectiveness.
• Ensure that academic programs and processes meet applicable U.S. and Swiss accreditation and quality-assurance requirements, including MSCHE, SAC, and AAQ frameworks.
• Play a central role in preparing institutional self-studies, accreditation reports, academic documentation, and other academic reporting. Academic Operations and Resource Stewardship
• Work with the Associate Deans to oversee academic operations, including the Registrar’s Office, course scheduling, academic calendar planning, catalog and policy administration, and academic records.
• Provide leadership for academic support functions, including the Library, Writing and Learning Center, digital pedagogy initiatives, and institutional research.
• Coordinate the Academic Affairs budget and collaborate with the President’s Cabinet on institutional planning and responsible allocation of academic resources.
• Support coordination among faculty committees, academic programs, administrative units, and student services in day-to-day academic matters. Continuing Education
• Support the development and management of continuing education initiatives that make Franklin’s educational mission accessible to additional audiences.
• Provide leadership for the continuation and orderly transition of existing executive education activities through their current program cycle. Academic Affairs Portfolio The Dean’s current portfolio includes the Associate Dean for Student Success, Associate Dean for Institutional Effectiveness, Registrar, Library Director, Academic Affairs Coordinator, Director of the Green Office, Coordinator of Digital Pedagogy Initiatives and the Writing and Learning Center, and academic Program Directors. Reporting relationships and responsibilities may be adjusted in consultation with the President to respond to institutional priorities and operational needs. Experience and Qualifications
• A terminal degree from an accredited institution in an appropriate discipline; academic accomplishments sufficient for appointment at the rank of full professor are preferred.
• Demonstrated experience in academic leadership within higher education, including collaborative decision-making and a commitment to shared governance.
• Deep familiarity with the U.S. residential liberal arts model, its pedagogical foundations, faculty roles, and student support expectations; experience as a faculty member or academic leader within a residential liberal arts institution is highly desirable.
• Experience with institutional accreditation, academic assessment, or higher education quality-assurance frameworks.
• Familiarity with, or a willingness to develop a strong understanding of, Swiss and European higher education, including expectations for research productivity, research funding, and institutional quality assurance.
• An ability to work constructively across disciplines and academic cultures and to balance academic vision with operational responsibilities.
• Knowledge of Italian, or willingness to learn the language, is an asset; knowledge of another Swiss national language is advantageous. How to Apply Please submit a curriculum vitae, a letter of interest addressing the responsibilities and qualifications described above, and contact information for three professional references. Applications and nominations are welcome. Send application materials to DAAsearch@fus.edu Review of applications will begin December 1, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled. The anticipated start date is July 2027. Equal Opportunity and Work Authorization Franklin Switzerland is committed to fostering an open, fair, diverse, and inclusive academic community. The institution welcomes applicants from different backgrounds and perspectives and considers qualified candidates without unlawful discrimination. Due to Swiss employment and work-permit requirements, applications from Swiss and EU nationals will receive priority in the evaluation process; applications from all qualified candidates are welcome.

descriptionByLocale.it:
Franklin Svizzera Fondato nel 1969, Franklin Svizzera è tra le prime istituzioni a portare il modello di arti liberali degli Stati Uniti in Europa. Situato a Sorengo, affacciato su Lugano e sul suo lago nella regione di lingua italiana della Svizzera, Franklin combina una comunità di apprendimento residenziale, piccole classi, stretto coinvolgimento docenti-studente, studio interdisciplinare e una prospettiva globale. Franklin è accreditato negli Stati Uniti dalla Commissione per l'istruzione superiore (MSCHE) e opera come istituto universitario accreditato all'interno del sistema di istruzione superiore svizzero. Una caratteristica distintiva del curriculum di Franklin è Academic Travel: gite di studio di progettazione di docenti e guidate dalla facoltà che collegano l'apprendimento in aula con esperienze internazionali, basate sul luogo. Integrato negli obiettivi e nella valutazione del corso, Academic Travel coinvolge gli studenti direttamente con i contesti storici, culturali, politici, ambientali e sociali che studiano. Franklin offre corsi di laurea e laurea e promuove una forte cultura dell'insegnamento, della borsa di studio e della collaborazione interdisciplinare. Come istituto universitario in Svizzera, Franklin si impegna a standard di ricerca, attività di sovvenzione esterna e garanzia di qualità accademica. Le sue offerte di laurea includono il Master of Arts in Sostenibilità e Trasformazione e il dottorato accreditato in Scienze Politiche. Franklin si occupa di strutture di qualità gestite da MSCHE, il Consiglio svizzero di accreditamento (SAC), e l'Agenzia svizzera di accreditamento e garanzia di qualità (AAQ). L'Opportunity Franklin Svizzera invita domande e candidature per la posizione di Dean of Academic Affairs (Chief Academic Officer), con un inizio previsto nel luglio 2027 per l'anno accademico 2027–28. Segnalandosi al Presidente e lavorando a stretto contatto con il Gabinetto del Presidente, il Decano guida i programmi accademici, le operazioni e le funzioni di supporto dell'istituzione e contribuisce alla sua direzione strategica. Franklin cerca un leader accademico collaborativo e avanzato che può far progredire il suo modello di arti liberali residenziali degli Stati Uniti, sostenendo al contempo la ricerca, la qualità e le aspettative istituzionali dell'istruzione superiore svizzera ed europea. Il Decano lavora a stretto contatto con enti di governo della facoltà, Dean associati, leadership del programma accademico e unità di supporto per promuovere l'eccellenza didattica, l'innovazione accademica, la borsa di studio della facoltà e il successo degli studenti. Il ruolo combina la leadership strategica con una sostanziale responsabilità amministrativa accademica quotidiana. Responsabilità chiave Leadership accademica e sviluppo curricolo
• Condurre lo sviluppo, la revisione periodica e la valorizzazione dei programmi accademici laureati e laureati, garantendo qualità accademica e allineamento con la missione di Franklin.
• Rafforzare il curriculum di arti liberali residenziali, il suo carattere interdisciplinare, e la sua enfasi sulla formazione attiva, studente-centro e esperienziale.
• Sostenere il continuo sviluppo e la piena integrazione accademica del programma di viaggio accademico di Franklin, compresi i suoi collegamenti ai risultati di apprendimento dei corsi.
• Guida proposte per nuovi programmi accademici e iniziative curriculari in risposta alle priorità istituzionali e alle esigenze educative emergenti. Sviluppo e Pedagogia della Facoltà
• Promuovi l'eccellenza dell'insegnamento attraverso lo sviluppo della facoltà nell'apprendimento delle arti liberali attive, progettazione di curriculum efficace e pedagogia concentrata sugli studenti.
• Incoraggiare approcci innovativi di insegnamento adatti a una comunità di apprendimento residenziale e diversificata.
• Promuovere la collaborazione interdisciplinare, lo scambio di docenti e una cultura accademica collegiale e intellettuale. Leadership della Facoltà e governance condivisa
• Collabora con gli organi di governo della facoltà e i comitati sulle politiche accademiche e sui processi di governo condiviso.
• supervisionare i processi di valutazione, promozione e sviluppo professionale in collaborazione con i comitati di facoltà appropriati.
• Fornire la leadership accademica e il supporto per il lavoro di facoltà, incoraggiando le relazioni produttive tra divisioni e programmi accademici. Successo degli studenti e supporto accademico
• Partner con il Decano Associato per il Successo degli Studenti e colleghi in tutta l'istituzione per rafforzare la consulenza, il sostegno all'apprendimento e le politiche accademiche che promuovono il successo degli studenti.
• Assicurare sistemi di supporto accademico efficaci, tra cui consulenza accademica, assistenza all'apprendimento e alloggi accademici appropriati, coerente con un ambiente di arti liberali residenziali in stile statunitense.
• Lavora con unità di supporto accademico e servizi per gli studenti per affrontare le preoccupazioni accademiche degli studenti e mantenere un ambiente di apprendimento reattivo e di supporto. Ricerca e Formazione Scholarly
• Sostenere una vivace cultura della ricerca e della borsa di studio di docenti su discipline, coerente con le aspettative di un istituto universitario svizzero e la più ampia comunità accademica internazionale.
• Incoraggiare le domande di finanziamento competitivo della ricerca, importanti sovvenzioni esterne e partnership di ricerca.
• Fornire leadership accademica per i programmi legati alla ricerca, tra cui Franklin accreditato PhD in Scienze Politiche.
• Promuovere la ricerca interdisciplinare che affronta le sfide globali, tra cui la sostenibilità e l'impatto sociale. Efficacia istituzionale e accreditamento
• Condurre la valutazione accademica, l'efficacia istituzionale e il miglioramento continuo informato delle prove in collaborazione con l'Associated Dean per l'Efficienza Istituzionale.
• Assicurarsi che i programmi e i processi accademici soddisfino i requisiti applicabili di accreditamento e di assicurazione della qualità, tra cui MSCHE, SAC e AAQ.
• Gioca un ruolo centrale nella preparazione di auto-studies istituzionali, rapporti di accreditamento, documentazione accademica e altri rapporti accademici. Operazioni accademiche e gestione delle risorse
• Lavorare con i Presidenti Associati per supervisionare le operazioni accademiche, tra cui l'Ufficio del Registratore, la pianificazione dei corsi, la pianificazione del calendario accademico, il catalogo e l'amministrazione politica e i registri accademici.
• Fornire la leadership per le funzioni di supporto accademico, tra cui la Biblioteca, Centro di scrittura e apprendimento, iniziative di pedagogia digitale, e la ricerca istituzionale.
• Coordinare il bilancio degli Affari Accademici e collaborare con il Gabinetto del Presidente sulla pianificazione istituzionale e sull’assegnazione responsabile delle risorse accademiche.
• Coordinamento di sostegno tra comitati di facoltà, programmi accademici, unità amministrative e servizi di studenti in materia accademica quotidiana. Formazione continua
• Sostenere lo sviluppo e la gestione di iniziative di formazione continua che rendono la missione educativa di Franklin accessibile a pubblico aggiuntivo.
• Fornire la leadership per la continuazione e la transizione ordinata delle attività di istruzione esecutiva esistenti attraverso il loro ciclo di programma attuale. Portfolio degli Affari Accademici L’attuale portafoglio del Decano comprende il Decano Associato per il Successo degli Studenti, Preside associato per l’Efficienza Istituzionale, il Registratore, il Direttore della Biblioteca, il Coordinatore degli Affari Accademici, il Direttore dell’Ufficio Verde, il Coordinatore delle Iniziative Digitali di Pedagogia e il Centro di Scrittura e Apprendimento e gli Amministratori del Programma Accademico. Le relazioni e le responsabilità di relazione possono essere regolate in consultazione con il Presidente per rispondere alle priorità istituzionali e alle esigenze operative. Esperienza e qualifiche
• Un grado terminale da un istituto accreditato in una disciplina appropriata; i risultati accademici sufficienti per l'appuntamento al rango di professore pieno sono preferiti.
• Esperienza dimostrata nella leadership accademica all'interno dell'istruzione superiore, tra cui il processo decisionale collaborativo e l'impegno per la governance condivisa.
• La profonda familiarità con il modello di arti liberali residenziali degli Stati Uniti, le sue basi pedagogiche, i ruoli di facoltà e le aspettative di sostegno degli studenti; l'esperienza come membro della facoltà o leader accademico all'interno di un istituto di arti residenziali liberali è altamente auspicabile.
• Esperienza con accreditamento istituzionale, valutazione accademica, o quadri di assicurazione della qualità dell'istruzione superiore.
• La familiarità con, o la volontà di sviluppare una forte comprensione dell'istruzione superiore svizzera ed europea, comprese le aspettative per la produttività della ricerca, il finanziamento della ricerca e l'assicurazione della qualità istituzionale.
• Una capacità di lavorare costruttivamente in discipline e culture accademiche e di bilanciare la visione accademica con responsabilità operative.
• La conoscenza dell'italiano, o la volontà di imparare la lingua, è un bene; la conoscenza di un'altra lingua nazionale svizzera è vantaggiosa. Come applicare Si prega di inviare un curriculum vitae, una lettera di interesse che affronta le responsabilità e le qualifiche sopra descritte, e le informazioni di contatto per tre riferimenti professionali. Le domande e le candidature sono benvenute. Invia materiale di applicazione a DAAsearch@fus.edu La revisione delle applicazioni inizierà il 1 dicembre 2026 e continuerà fino a quando la posizione sarà riempita. La data di inizio prevista è luglio 2027. Franklin Svizzera si impegna a promuovere una comunità accademica aperta, equa, diversificata e inclusiva. L'istituzione accoglie i candidati provenienti da diversi background e prospettive e considera i candidati qualificati senza discriminazione illecita. A causa dei requisiti di occupazione e di lavoro svizzeri, le domande di cittadini svizzeri e UE riceveranno la priorità nel processo di valutazione; le domande di tutti i candidati qualificati sono benvenuti.

Franklin Switzerland wurde 1969 gegründet und gehört zu den ersten Institutionen, die das US-amerikanische Modell der freien Künste nach Europa bringen. In Sorengo gelegen, mit Blick auf Lugano und seinen See in der italienischsprachigen Region der Schweiz, kombiniert Franklin eine Wohn-Lerngemeinschaft, kleine Klassen, enges Dozenten-Studenten-Engagement, interdisziplinäres Studium und eine globale Perspektive. Franklin ist in den Vereinigten Staaten von der Middle States Commission on Higher Education (MSCHE) akkreditiert und arbeitet als akkreditiertes Universitätsinstitut im Schweizer Hochschulsystem. Ein definierendes Merkmal von Franklins Curriculum ist Academic Travel: von Fakultäten entworfene und von Fakultäten geleitete Studienreisen, die das Lernen im Klassenzimmer mit internationalen, ortsbezogenen Erfahrungen verbinden. Integriert in Kursziele und Bewertung, Akademisches Reisen engagiert die Studierenden direkt mit den historischen, kulturellen, politischen, ökologischen und sozialen Kontexten, die sie studieren. Franklin bietet Bachelor- und Graduiertenprogramme an und fördert eine starke Kultur der Lehre, des Stipendiums und der interdisziplinären Zusammenarbeit. Als Universitätsinstitut in der Schweiz engagiert sich Franklin für Forschungsstandards, externe Förderaktivitäten und akademische Qualitätssicherung. Zu den Diplom-Angeboten gehören der Master of Arts in Nachhaltigkeit und Transformation und der in der Schweiz akkreditierte PhD in Politikwissenschaft. Franklin arbeitet mit Qualitätsrahmen zusammen, die von MSCHE, dem Swiss Accreditation Council (SAC) und der Swiss Agency of Accreditation and Quality Assurance (AAQ) verwaltet werden. Die Gelegenheit Franklin Schweiz lädt Bewerbungen und Nominierungen für die Position des Dekans für akademische Angelegenheiten (Chief Academic Officer) ein, mit einem erwarteten Start im Juli 2027 für das akademische Jahr 2027-28. Der Dekan, der dem Präsidenten berichtet und eng mit dem Kabinett des Präsidenten zusammenarbeitet, leitet die akademischen Programme, Operationen und Unterstützungsfunktionen der Institution und trägt zu ihrer strategischen Ausrichtung bei. Franklin sucht einen kollaborativen, zukunftsweisenden akademischen Führer, der sein US-amerikanisches Wohnmodell für freie Künste voranbringen und gleichzeitig die Forschung, Qualität und institutionellen Erwartungen der Schweizer und europäischen Hochschulbildung unterstützen kann. Der Dekan arbeitet eng mit Fakultäts-Governance-Gremien, Associate Deans, akademischen Programmführung und Unterstützung Einheiten Lehre Exzellenz, akademische Innovation, Fakultät Stipendium und Schüler Erfolg zu fördern. Die Rolle verbindet strategische Führung mit erheblichen Tag-zu-Tag akademische administrative Verantwortung. Wichtige Aufgaben Akademische Führung und Curriculum Entwicklung
• Führen Sie die Entwicklung, regelmäßige Überprüfung und Verbesserung von Grund- und Hochschulprogrammen, um die akademische Qualität und Ausrichtung auf Franklins Mission zu gewährleisten.
• Stärken Sie den Lehrplan für wohnfreie Künste, seinen interdisziplinären Charakter und seinen Schwerpunkt auf aktiver, studentenzentrierter und experimenteller Bildung.
• Unterstützen Sie die weitere Entwicklung und vollständige akademische Integration von Franklins Signatur Academic Travel-Programm, einschließlich seiner Verbindungen zu Kurslernergebnissen.
• Leitfadenvorschläge für neue akademische Programme und curriculare Initiativen als Reaktion auf institutionelle Prioritäten und aufkommende Bildungsbedürfnisse. Fakultätsentwicklung und Pädagogik
• Fördern Sie die Lehre Exzellenz durch Fakultät Entwicklung in aktiven liberalen Künsten Lernen, effektive Curriculum-Design und Studenten-zentrierte Pädagogik.
• Förderung innovativer Lehransätze, die für eine vielfältige, internationale Wohngemeinschaft geeignet sind.
• Fördern Sie interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit, Fakultätsaustausch und eine kollegiale und intellektuell engagierte akademische Kultur. Faculty Leadership und Shared Governance
• Zusammenarbeit mit Fakultäts-Governance-Gremien und -Ausschüssen zu akademischen Richtlinien und geteilten Governance-Prozessen.
• Beaufsichtigen Fakultät Bewertung, Förderung und berufliche Entwicklungsprozesse in Partnerschaft mit den entsprechenden Fakultätsausschüssen.
• Bieten Sie akademische Führung und Unterstützung für die Arbeit der Fakultät, während Sie produktive Beziehungen zwischen akademischen Abteilungen und Programmen fördern. Studentischer Erfolg und akademische Unterstützung
• Partnerschaft mit dem Associate Dean for Student Success und Kollegen in der gesamten Institution, um Beratung, Lernunterstützung und akademische Richtlinien zu stärken, die den Erfolg der Schüler fördern.
• Gewährleistung effektiver akademischer Unterstützungssysteme, einschließlich akademischer Beratung, Lernunterstützung und geeigneter akademischer Unterkünfte, die mit einer Wohnumgebung im US-Stil im Einklang stehen.
• Arbeiten Sie mit akademischen Unterstützungseinheiten und Studentendiensten zusammen, um die akademischen Belange der Schüler anzugehen und eine ansprechende, unterstützende Lernumgebung zu erhalten. Forschung und wissenschaftliche Engagement
• Unterstützung einer lebendigen Kultur der Fakultätsforschung und -stipendien über Disziplinen hinweg, die den Erwartungen eines Schweizer Universitätsinstituts und der breiteren internationalen akademischen Gemeinschaft entspricht.
• Förderung von Anträgen auf wettbewerbsfähige Forschungsfinanzierung, bedeutende externe Zuschüsse und Forschungspartnerschaften.
• Bieten Sie akademische Führung für forschungsbezogene Programme, einschließlich Franklins in der Schweiz akkreditierten PhD in Politikwissenschaft.
• Förderung interdisziplinärer Forschung zur Bewältigung globaler Herausforderungen, einschließlich Nachhaltigkeit und sozialer Auswirkungen. Institutionelle Wirksamkeit und Akkreditierung
• Führen Sie akademische Bewertung, institutionelle Wirksamkeit und evidenzbasierte kontinuierliche Verbesserung in Partnerschaft mit dem Associate Dean for Institutional Effectiveness.
• Stellen Sie sicher, dass akademische Programme und Prozesse die geltenden Akkreditierungs- und Qualitätssicherungsanforderungen der USA und der Schweiz erfüllen, einschließlich MSCHE-, SAC- und AAQ-Rahmen.
• Spielen Sie eine zentrale Rolle bei der Vorbereitung institutioneller Selbststudien, Akkreditierungsberichte, wissenschaftliche Dokumentation und andere akademische Berichterstattung. Academic Operations und Resource Stewardship
• Arbeiten Sie mit den Associate Deans zusammen, um akademische Operationen zu überwachen, einschließlich des Registrar's Office, Kursplanung, akademische Kalenderplanung, Katalog- und Richtlinienverwaltung sowie akademische Aufzeichnungen.
• Führen Sie akademische Unterstützungsfunktionen, einschließlich Bibliothek, Schreib- und Lernzentrum, Initiativen für digitale Pädagogik und institutionelle Forschung.
• Koordinieren Sie das Budget für akademische Angelegenheiten und arbeiten Sie mit dem Kabinett des Präsidenten bei der institutionellen Planung und der verantwortungsvollen Zuweisung von akademischen Ressourcen zusammen.
• Unterstützen Sie die Koordination zwischen Fakultätsausschüssen, akademischen Programmen, Verwaltungseinheiten und Studentendiensten in alltäglichen akademischen Angelegenheiten. Weiterbildung
• Unterstützen Sie die Entwicklung und das Management von Weiterbildungsinitiativen, die Franklins Bildungsmission für zusätzliche Zielgruppen zugänglich machen.
• Führung für die Fortsetzung und den geordneten Übergang bestehender Executive Education-Aktivitäten durch ihren aktuellen Programmzyklus. Portfolio für akademische Angelegenheiten Das aktuelle Portfolio des Dekans umfasst den Associate Dean for Student Success, Associate Dean for Institutional Effectiveness, Registrar, Library Director, Academic Affairs Coordinator, Director des Green Office, Coordinator of Digital Pedagogy Initiatives und das Writing and Learning Center sowie akademische Programmdirektoren. Berichterstattungsbeziehungen und Verantwortlichkeiten können in Absprache mit dem Präsidenten angepasst werden, um den institutionellen Prioritäten und operativen Erfordernissen gerecht zu werden. Erfahrung und Qualifikationen
• Ein Abschlussabschluss einer akkreditierten Institution in einer geeigneten Disziplin; akademische Leistungen, die für die Ernennung zum ordentlichen Professor ausreichen, werden bevorzugt.
• Nachgewiesene Erfahrung in der akademischen Führung in der Hochschulbildung, einschließlich kollaborativer Entscheidungsfindung und einer Verpflichtung zu gemeinsamer Governance.
• Tiefe Vertrautheit mit dem US-amerikanischen Wohn-Liberal Arts-Modell, seinen pädagogischen Stiftungen, Fakultätsrollen und Erwartungen an die Schülerunterstützung; Erfahrung als Fakultätsmitglied oder akademischer Leiter innerhalb einer Wohn-Liberal Arts-Institution ist sehr wünschenswert.
• Erfahrung mit institutioneller Akkreditierung, akademischer Bewertung oder Hochschulqualitätssicherungsrahmen.
• Vertrautheit mit oder Bereitschaft, ein starkes Verständnis der schweizerischen und europäischen Hochschulbildung zu entwickeln, einschließlich Erwartungen an die Forschungsproduktivität, Forschungsfinanzierung und institutionelle Qualitätssicherung.
• Eine Fähigkeit, konstruktiv über Disziplinen und akademische Kulturen zu arbeiten und akademische Vision mit operativen Verantwortlichkeiten in Einklang zu bringen.
• Italienischkenntnisse oder die Bereitschaft, die Sprache zu lernen, sind von Vorteil; Kenntnisse einer anderen Schweizer Landessprache sind von Vorteil. Bitte reichen Sie einen Lebenslauf, ein Schreiben von Interesse, das die oben beschriebenen Verantwortlichkeiten und Qualifikationen anspricht, und Kontaktinformationen für drei professionelle Referenzen ein. Bewerbungen und Nominierungen sind willkommen. Senden Sie Bewerbungsunterlagen an DAAsearch@fus.edu Die Überprüfung der Bewerbungen beginnt am 1. Dezember 2026 und wird fortgesetzt, bis die Position besetzt ist. Das voraussichtliche Startdatum ist Juli 2027. À propos de Franklin Suisse Fondée en 1969, Franklin Suisse est l'une des premières institutions à apporter le modèle des arts libéraux américains en Europe. Situé à Sorengo, surplombant Lugano et son lac dans la région italophone de Suisse, Franklin combine une communauté d'apprentissage résidentiel, de petites classes, un engagement proche du corps professoral, des études interdisciplinaires et une perspective globale. Franklin est accrédité aux États-Unis par la Middle States Commission on Higher Education (MSCHE) et fonctionne comme un institut universitaire accrédité au sein du système d'enseignement supérieur suisse. Un élément déterminant du programme Franklin est Voyages académiques : voyages d'études conçus et dirigés par le corps professoral qui relient l'apprentissage en classe à des expériences internationales basées sur des lieux. Intégré aux objectifs et à l'évaluation des cours, Academic Travel engage directement les étudiants dans les contextes historiques, culturels, politiques, environnementaux et sociaux qu'ils étudient. Franklin offre des programmes de premier cycle et de deuxième cycle et favorise une solide culture d'enseignement, de bourses et de collaboration interdisciplinaire. En tant qu'institut universitaire en Suisse, Franklin s'engage à respecter les normes de recherche, les subventions externes et l'assurance de la qualité académique. Ses offres d'études supérieures comprennent la maîtrise ès arts en durabilité et transformation et le doctorat en sciences politiques accrédité en Suisse. Franklin collabore avec des cadres de qualité administrés par MSCHE, le Conseil suisse d'accréditation (SAC) et l'Agence suisse d'accréditation et d'assurance de la qualité (AAQ). L'Opportunity Franklin Suisse invite les candidats et les candidats au poste de doyen des affaires académiques (Chef des affaires académiques), avec un début prévu en juillet 2027 pour l'année académique 2027–2028. Relevant du président et travaillant en étroite collaboration avec le Cabinet du président, le doyen dirige les programmes universitaires, les opérations et les fonctions de soutien de l'institution et contribue à son orientation stratégique. Franklin cherche un leader académique collaboratif et tourné vers l'avenir qui peut faire progresser son modèle d'arts libéraux résidentiels américains tout en soutenant la recherche, la qualité et les attentes institutionnelles de l'enseignement supérieur suisse et européen. Le doyen travaille en étroite collaboration avec les organismes de gouvernance du corps professoral, les doyens associés, le leadership des programmes universitaires et les unités de soutien pour promouvoir l'excellence de l'enseignement, l'innovation universitaire, les bourses du corps professoral et la réussite des étudiants. Ce rôle combine le leadership stratégique et une importante responsabilité administrative académique quotidienne. Principales responsabilités Leadership académique et élaboration des programmes
• Diriger l'élaboration, l'examen périodique et l'amélioration des programmes universitaires de premier et de deuxième cycle, en assurant la qualité académique et l'alignement avec la mission Franklin.
• Renforcer le programme d'arts libéraux résidentiels, son caractère interdisciplinaire et son accent sur l'éducation active, centrée sur les étudiants et l'expérience.
• Appuyer le développement continu et l'intégration complète du programme de voyage académique signé Franklin, y compris ses liens avec les résultats d'apprentissage des cours.
• Guider les propositions de nouveaux programmes d'études et de nouvelles initiatives de programmes d'études en réponse aux priorités institutionnelles et aux nouveaux besoins éducatifs. Développement des facultés et pédagogie
• Promouvoir l'excellence de l'enseignement par le développement du corps professoral dans l'apprentissage actif des arts libéraux, la conception efficace des programmes et la pédagogie axée sur les étudiants.
• Encourager des approches pédagogiques novatrices adaptées à une communauté d'apprentissage diversifiée, internationale et résidentielle.
• Favoriser la collaboration interdisciplinaire, l'échange de professeurs et une culture universitaire collégiale et intellectuellement engagée. Leadership du corps professoral et gouvernance partagée
• Collaborer avec les organismes de gouvernance du corps professoral et les comités sur les politiques universitaires et les processus de gouvernance partagée.
• Superviser les processus d'évaluation, de promotion et de perfectionnement professionnel du corps professoral en partenariat avec les comités appropriés du corps professoral.
• Fournir un leadership et un soutien académiques pour le travail du corps professoral, tout en encourageant les relations productives entre les divisions et les programmes universitaires. Succès des étudiants et soutien scolaire
• Établir des partenariats avec le doyen associé à la réussite étudiante et les collègues de l'établissement pour renforcer les conseils, le soutien à l'apprentissage et les politiques scolaires qui favorisent la réussite étudiante.
• Assurer des systèmes de soutien scolaire efficaces, y compris des conseils universitaires, de l'aide à l'apprentissage et des aménagements scolaires appropriés, conformément à un milieu des arts libéraux résidentiels de style américain.
• Travailler avec les unités de soutien scolaire et les services aux étudiants pour répondre aux préoccupations des étudiants et maintenir un environnement d'apprentissage réceptif et favorable. Recherche et engagement des chercheurs
• Soutenir une culture dynamique de recherche et de bourses entre les disciplines, conformément aux attentes d'un institut universitaire suisse et de la communauté universitaire internationale.
• Encourager les demandes de financement concurrentiel de la recherche, les grandes subventions externes et les partenariats de recherche.
• Fournir un leadership académique pour les programmes liés à la recherche, y compris Franklin , Ph.D. en sciences politiques.
• Promouvoir la recherche interdisciplinaire sur les défis mondiaux, y compris la durabilité et l'impact social. Efficacité institutionnelle et accréditation
• Diriger l'évaluation universitaire, l'efficacité institutionnelle et l'amélioration continue fondée sur des données probantes en partenariat avec le doyen associé pour l'efficacité institutionnelle.
• Veiller à ce que les programmes et les processus universitaires répondent aux exigences applicables en matière d'accréditation et d'assurance de la qualité aux États-Unis et en Suisse, y compris les cadres MSCHE, SAC et AAQ.
• Jouer un rôle central dans la préparation des auto-études institutionnelles, des rapports d'accréditation, de la documentation universitaire et d'autres rapports universitaires. Activités universitaires et gérance des ressources
• Collaborer avec les doyens associés pour superviser les opérations universitaires, y compris le bureau du registraire, l'horaire des cours, la planification du calendrier scolaire, le catalogue et l'administration des politiques, et les dossiers universitaires.
• Fournir un leadership pour les fonctions d'appui académique, y compris la Bibliothèque, le Centre d'écriture et d'apprentissage, les initiatives de pédagogie numérique et la recherche institutionnelle.
• Coordonner le budget des affaires académiques et collaborer avec le Cabinet du Président sur la planification institutionnelle et l'allocation responsable des ressources académiques.
• Appuyer la coordination entre les comités du corps professoral, les programmes universitaires, les unités administratives et les services aux étudiants en matière d'enseignement quotidien. Formation continue
• Appuyer l'élaboration et la gestion d'initiatives de formation continue qui rendent la mission éducative de Franklin accessible à d'autres publics.
• Assurer le leadership en vue de la poursuite et de la transition ordonnée des activités de formation des cadres dans le cadre de leur cycle de programme actuel. Portefeuille des affaires universitaires Le portefeuille actuel du doyen comprend le doyen associé pour la réussite étudiante, le doyen associé pour l'efficacité institutionnelle, le registraire, le directeur de la bibliothèque, le coordonnateur des affaires universitaires, le directeur du Bureau vert, le coordonnateur des initiatives de pédagogie numérique et le Centre d'écriture et d'apprentissage, et les directeurs de programmes universitaires. Les relations et les responsabilités en matière de rapports peuvent être ajustées en consultation avec le président afin de répondre aux priorités institutionnelles et aux besoins opérationnels. Expérience et qualifications
• Un diplôme de fin d'études d'un établissement accrédité dans une discipline appropriée; les réalisations scolaires suffisantes pour être nommées au grade de professeur titulaire sont préférées.
• Expérience démontrée du leadership universitaire dans l'enseignement supérieur, y compris la prise de décisions en collaboration et l'engagement en faveur d'une gouvernance partagée.
• Connaissance approfondie du modèle des arts libéraux résidentiels des États-Unis, de ses fondements pédagogiques, de ses rôles dans le corps professoral et de ses attentes en matière de soutien aux étudiants.
• Expérience de l'accréditation institutionnelle, de l'évaluation académique ou des cadres d'assurance de la qualité de l'enseignement supérieur.
• Connaissance de l'enseignement supérieur suisse et européen, ou volonté de développer une solide compréhension de l'enseignement supérieur suisse et européen, y compris les attentes en matière de productivité de la recherche, de financement de la recherche et d'assurance qualité institutionnelle.
• Capacité de travailler de façon constructive dans les disciplines et les cultures universitaires et d'équilibrer la vision académique et les responsabilités opérationnelles.
• La connaissance de l'italien, ou la volonté d'apprendre la langue, est un atout; la connaissance d'une autre langue nationale suisse est avantageuse. Comment faire une demande Veuillez soumettre un curriculum vitae, une lettre d'intérêt portant sur les responsabilités et les qualifications décrites ci-dessus, ainsi que les coordonnées de trois références professionnelles. Les candidatures et les candidatures sont les bienvenues. Envoyer le matériel d'application à DAAsearch@fus.edu L'examen des demandes commencera le 1er décembre 2026 et se poursuivra jusqu'à ce que le poste soit comblé. La date de début prévue est juillet 2027. Égalité des chances et autorisation de travail Franklin Suisse s'engage à favoriser une communauté universitaire ouverte, équitable, diversifiée et inclusive. L'institution accueille les candidats de différents horizons et points de vue et considère les candidats qualifiés sans discrimination illégale. En raison des exigences suisses en matière d'emploi et de permis de travail, les candidatures de ressortissants suisses et de ressortissants de l'UE recevront la priorité dans le processus d'évaluation; les candidatures de tous les candidats qualifiés sont les bienvenues.

jobs.description:
Executive Assistant, Office of the President Franklin Switzerland · Office of the President · Lugano, Switzerland Reports to: President · Position type: Part-time (50%-70%; 20-28 hours per week), on-campus About Franklin Switzerland Franklin Switzerland, founded in 1969, is one of the first institutions to bring liberal arts education to Europe and to be recognized by both U.S. and Swiss accreditation agencies. A leader in international education, Franklin provides an experiential and multinational learning environment through small classes, strong student and faculty relationships, a residential campus, and hands-on Academic Travel experiences. With roughly 300 students from more than 60 countries, set in the safe and striking landscape of Lugano, Franklin is distinctive: an intimate residential community, a uniquely dual U.S.-Swiss accreditation, and an Academic Travel program that turns the world into a classroom. Franklin promotes intellectual curiosity and critical thinking, strives for academic excellence, and fosters interdisciplinary opportunities for its students, faculty, and staff. Franklin acknowledges the accomplishments and global impact of our community through a culture of trust that respects diversity, equity, inclusion, and continuous improvement. The Opportunity Franklin Switzerland is seeking an organized, proactive, and highly discreet Executive Assistant to provide administrative, operational, and organizational support to the Office of the President. Serving as the administrative hub for executive operations, the position helps coordinate communications, scheduling, travel, meetings, Board administration, and institutional processes so that executive priorities can move forward efficiently and reliably. Working closely with the President, the Board of Trustees, and colleagues across the institution, the Executive Assistant will also support selected institution-wide initiatives, including Advancement, institutional effectiveness, accreditation, and special projects. 
• Responsibilities will vary throughout the academic year in response to the institutional calendar and operational priorities. This role is well suited to a service-oriented professional who enjoys working across multiple functions, exercises sound judgment and discretion, communicates confidently in both English and Italian, and thrives in a collaborative, international university environment. Key 
• Responsibilities Executive Coordination & Office Administration ▪ Manage the President's calendar, appointments, and scheduling priorities. ▪ Coordinate meetings with internal and external stakeholders, preparing agendas, meeting materials, and follow-up communications in both English and Italian. ▪ Draft, edit, format, and distribute correspondence, reports, presentations, and other executive documents in both English and Italian. ▪ Manage incoming inquiries to the Office of the President, exercising sound judgment in prioritizing matters requiring the President's attention. ▪ Coordinate domestic and international travel, including itineraries, accommodations, visas where required, and related documentation. ▪ Prepare travel expenses and reimbursements. ▪ Track projects, requests, deadlines, and action items on behalf of the Office of the President, ensuring timely follow-up across institutional offices. ▪ Maintain confidential records and serve as the primary administrative contact for the Office of the President. Board of Trustees Administration ▪ Serve as the principal administrative support for the Board of Trustees and its committees. ▪ Coordinate the annual calendar of Board and committee meetings in collaboration with the President, Secretary to the Board, Board Chair, and committee chairs. ▪ Schedule meetings and manage meeting logistics, invitations, attendance, and materials. ▪ Prepare, distribute, and archive Board agendas, minutes, supporting documentation, and official records. ▪ Maintain Board document repositories and ensure trustees have timely access to meeting materials. ▪ Coordinate trustee travel, accommodations, reimbursements, and related logistics. ▪ Serve as the primary administrative liaison for trustees regarding meeting schedules, travel, Board materials, and other administrative matters. ▪ Support the Secretary to the Board by managing the administrative and logistical aspects of Board operations, enabling the Secretary to focus on governance, policy, Board development, and strategic matters. Advancement & Institutional Events ▪ Support presidential and Advancement events by coordinating invitations, registrations, venues, catering, travel arrangements, audiovisual requirements, and event materials. ▪ Prepare event communications and participant correspondence in both English and Italian. ▪ Assist with donor, alumni, trustee, and institutional events sponsored by the Office of the President or the Office of Advancement. ▪ Assist with the planning and delivery of the annual Commencement ceremony and surrounding events. Institutional Effectiveness & Accreditation Support ▪ Provide administrative support for institutional effectiveness, planning, and accreditation activities through document management, data coordination, evidence management, survey administration, and related administrative processes. ▪ Assist with the collection and organization of institutional data from academic and administrative units. ▪ Maintain archives of institutional reports, supporting documentation, and historical records. ▪ Assist in preparing recurring institutional reports and responding to institutional data requests. ▪ Coordinate institutional surveys and related administrative processes. ▪ Support accreditation and quality assurance through evidence management, document organization, and tracking. ▪ Maintain the MSCHE Self-Study evidence repository and coordinate evidence requests across Franklin offices. ▪ Assist in developing efficient administrative processes that support institutional reporting, assessment, and accreditation activities. Office Operations ▪ Welcome visitors to the Office of the President and respond to inquiries in both English and Italian. ▪ Answer and direct telephone calls for the Office of the President and provide concurrent reception coverage as operational needs require. ▪ Maintain office records, filing systems, and administrative procedures. ▪ Support special projects and perform other duties consistent with the responsibilities of the Office of the President and the institution's mission. Experience and 
• Qualifications The successful candidate will combine strong administrative skills with sound judgment, discretion, and a service-oriented approach. The following qualifications are expected: ▪ Education and professional preparation — A commercial apprenticeship (EFZ), higher vocational qualification, bachelor's degree, or equivalent professional preparation. ▪ Relevant experience — At least three years of progressively responsible administrative or executive support experience, preferably supporting senior leadership. ▪ Organization and coordination — Excellent organizational, planning, and project and process coordination skills, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines, and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment. ▪ Communication — Exceptional written and verbal communication skills in both English and Italian. ▪ Judgment and confidentiality — Ability to exercise sound judgment, maintain strict confidentiality, and handle sensitive information with discretion. ▪ Relationship management — Strong interpersonal skills and a professional, service-oriented approach to colleagues, trustees, visitors, and external stakeholders. ▪ Technology — Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and standard office technologies. ▪ Initiative and adaptability — Ability to work independently, take initiative, solve problems, and adapt to changing priorities. Preferred Experience ▪ Experience in higher education, nonprofit, or international organizations. ▪ Experience supporting executive leadership and/or governing boards. ▪ Experience coordinating institutional or donor events. ▪ Familiarity with CRM, survey, or institutional information systems (e.g., Slate, Qualtrics, or similar platforms), together with skill in Excel and other reporting tools. ▪ Experience supporting accreditation, assessment, or institutional effectiveness initiatives. Competencies and personal qualities ▪ Organization and planning ▪ Professional judgment and discretion ▪ Clear, effective communication ▪ Relationship management ▪ Project and process coordination ▪ Service orientation ▪ Adaptability and flexibility ▪ Attention to detail ▪ Problem solving ▪ Digital literacy How to Apply For consideration by the search committee, candidates are asked to submit the following documents in PDF format at EAsearch@fus.edu: ▪ A current CV detailing relevant experience; ▪ A letter of interest that addresses the key areas of this job description; ▪ Contact information for three references, two of which must be former direct supervisors; Please note that, due to Swiss visa and work-permit regulations, applications from Swiss or EU nationals will be given priority in the evaluation process.

Executive Assistant, Office of the President Franklin Switzerland · Office of the President · Lugano, Svizzera Reports to: President · Tipo di posizione: Part-time (50%-70%; 20-28 ore a settimana), on-campus About Franklin Switzerland Franklin Switzerland, fondata nel 1969, è una delle prime istituzioni a portare l'educazione alle arti liberali in Europa e ad essere riconosciuta da agenzie di accreditamento statunitensi e svizzeri. Leader nell'educazione internazionale, Franklin fornisce un ambiente di apprendimento esperienziale e multinazionale attraverso piccole classi, forti rapporti studenteschi e docenti, un campus residenziale, e esperienze pratiche di viaggio accademico. Con circa 300 studenti provenienti da più di 60 paesi, ambientati nel paesaggio sicuro e suggestivo di Lugano, Franklin è caratteristico: un'intima comunità residenziale, un'accreditamento dual U.S.-Swiss e un programma di viaggio accademico che trasforma il mondo in classe. Franklin promuove la curiosità intellettuale e il pensiero critico, si sforza per l'eccellenza accademica, e promuove opportunità interdisciplinari per i suoi studenti, docenti e personale. Franklin riconosce i risultati e l'impatto globale della nostra comunità attraverso una cultura di fiducia che rispetta la diversità, l'equità, l'inclusione e il miglioramento continuo. L'Opportunità Franklin Svizzera sta cercando un assistente esecutivo organizzato, proattivo e altamente discreto per fornire supporto amministrativo, operativo e organizzativo all'Ufficio del Presidente. Servendo come hub amministrativo per le operazioni esecutive, la posizione aiuta a coordinare comunicazioni, pianificazione, viaggi, riunioni, amministrazione del Consiglio e processi istituzionali in modo che le priorità esecutive possano andare avanti in modo efficiente e affidabile. Lavorando a stretto contatto con il Presidente, il Consiglio di Amministrazione e i colleghi di tutta l'istituzione, l'Assistente Esecutivo sosterrà anche iniziative selezionate a livello istituzionale, tra cui Avanzamento, efficacia istituzionale, accreditamento e progetti speciali.
• Le responsabilità variano durante tutto l'anno accademico in risposta al calendario istituzionale e alle priorità operative. Questo ruolo è adatto a un professionista orientato al servizio che gode di lavorare in più funzioni, esercita giudizio e discrezione sonori, comunica con fiducia sia in inglese che in italiano, e prospera in un ambiente universitario collaborativo e internazionale. chiave

Executive Assistant, Office of the President Franklin Switzerland · Office of the President · Lugano, Switzerland Reports to: President · Position type: Part-time (50%-70%; 20-28 hours per week), on-campus About Franklin Switzerland Franklin Switzerland, founded in 1969, is one of the first institutions to bring liberal arts education to Europe and to be recognized by both U.S. and Swiss accreditation agencies. A leader in international education, Franklin provides an experiential and multinational learning environment through small classes, strong student and faculty relationships, a residential campus, and hands-on Academic Travel experiences. With roughly 300 students from more than 60 countries, set in the safe and striking landscape of Lugano, Franklin is distinctive: an intimate residential community, a uniquely dual U.S.-Swiss accreditation, and an Academic Travel program that turns the world into a classroom. Franklin promotes intellectual curiosity and critical thinking, strives for academic excellence, and fosters interdisciplinary opportunities for its students, faculty, and staff. Franklin acknowledges the accomplishments and global impact of our community through a culture of trust that respects diversity, equity, inclusion, and continuous improvement. The Opportunity Franklin Switzerland is seeking an organized, proactive, and highly discreet Executive Assistant to provide administrative, operational, and organizational support to the Office of the President. Serving as the administrative hub for executive operations, the position helps coordinate communications, scheduling, travel, meetings, Board administration, and institutional processes so that executive priorities can move forward efficiently and reliably. Working closely with the President, the Board of Trustees, and colleagues across the institution, the Executive Assistant will also support selected institution-wide initiatives, including Advancement, institutional effectiveness, accreditation, and special projects. 
• Responsibilities will vary throughout the academic year in response to the institutional calendar and operational priorities. This role is well suited to a service-oriented professional who enjoys working across multiple functions, exercises sound judgment and discretion, communicates confidently in both English and Italian, and thrives in a collaborative, international university environment. Key 
• Responsibilities Executive Coordination & Office Administration ▪ Manage the President's calendar, appointments, and scheduling priorities. ▪ Coordinate meetings with internal and external stakeholders, preparing agendas, meeting materials, and follow-up communications in both English and Italian. ▪ Draft, edit, format, and distribute correspondence, reports, presentations, and other executive documents in both English and Italian. ▪ Manage incoming inquiries to the Office of the President, exercising sound judgment in prioritizing matters requiring the President's attention. ▪ Coordinate domestic and international travel, including itineraries, accommodations, visas where required, and related documentation. ▪ Prepare travel expenses and reimbursements. ▪ Track projects, requests, deadlines, and action items on behalf of the Office of the President, ensuring timely follow-up across institutional offices. ▪ Maintain confidential records and serve as the primary administrative contact for the Office of the President. Advancement & Institutional Events ▪ Support presidential and Advancement events by coordinating invitations, registrations, venues, catering, travel arrangements, audiovisual requirements, and event materials. ▪ Prepare event communications and participant correspondence in both English and Italian. ▪ Assist with donor, alumni, trustee, and institutional events sponsored by the Office of the President or the Office of Advancement. ▪ Assist with the planning and delivery of the annual Commencement ceremony and surrounding events. Institutional Effectiveness & Accreditation Support ▪ Provide administrative support for institutional effectiveness, planning, and accreditation activities through document management, data coordination, evidence management, survey administration, and related administrative processes. ▪ Assist with the collection and organization of institutional data from academic and administrative units. ▪ Maintain archives of institutional reports, supporting documentation, and historical records. ▪ Assist in preparing recurring institutional reports and responding to institutional data requests. ▪ Coordinate institutional surveys and related administrative processes. ▪ Support accreditation and quality assurance through evidence management, document organization, and tracking. ▪ Maintain the MSCHE Self-Study evidence repository and coordinate evidence requests across Franklin offices. ▪ Assist in developing efficient administrative processes that support institutional reporting, assessment, and accreditation activities. Office Operations ▪ Welcome visitors to the Office of the President and respond to inquiries in both English and Italian. ▪ Answer and direct telephone calls for the Office of the President and provide concurrent reception coverage as operational needs require. ▪ Maintain office records, filing systems, and administrative procedures. ▪ Support special projects and perform other duties consistent with the responsibilities of the Office of the President and the institution's mission. Experience and 
• Qualifications The successful candidate will combine strong administrative skills with sound judgment, discretion, and a service-oriented approach. The following qualifications are expected: ▪ Education and professional preparation — A commercial apprenticeship (EFZ), higher vocational qualification, bachelor's degree, or equivalent professional preparation. ▪ Relevant experience — At least three years of progressively responsible administrative or executive support experience, preferably supporting senior leadership. ▪ Organization and coordination — Excellent organizational, planning, and project and process coordination skills, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines, and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment. ▪ Communication — Exceptional written and verbal communication skills in both English and Italian. ▪ Judgment and confidentiality — Ability to exercise sound judgment, maintain strict confidentiality, and handle sensitive information with discretion. ▪ Relationship management — Strong interpersonal skills and a professional, service-oriented approach to colleagues, trustees, visitors, and external stakeholders. ▪ Technology — Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and standard office technologies. ▪ Initiative and adaptability — Ability to work independently, take initiative, solve problems, and adapt to changing priorities. Preferred Experience ▪ Experience in higher education, nonprofit, or international organizations. ▪ Experience supporting executive leadership and/or governing boards. ▪ Experience coordinating institutional or donor events. ▪ Familiarity with CRM, survey, or institutional information systems (e.g., Slate, Qualtrics, or similar platforms), together with skill in Excel and other reporting tools. ▪ Experience supporting accreditation, assessment, or institutional effectiveness initiatives.
